title: The Viral Air Fryer Apple Cider Donuts Hack You Need Right Now
description: Make these insanely easy air fryer apple cider donuts in 10 minutes flat. No yeast, zero hassle, and only one basket to wash in my tiny apartment kitchen.
story: Look, I love a crisp autumn morning just as much as the next person, but standing over a vat of boiling oil in my tiny apartment kitchen to fry donuts? Hard pass. By the time I’m done, my living room smells like a deep fryer for three days and I’m staring down a greasy mess of pans with zero dishwasher space. I needed a weekday morning win that didn't involve a massive cleanup or waiting around for yeast to rise. That’s when I tested this absolute cheat code using canned biscuits and apple cider reduction. Full disclosure: the first time I tried this, I didn't reduce the cider enough and my dough turned into a soggy disaster. Lesson learned! Simmer that cider down first. Now, these air fryer apple cider donuts come together in 10 minutes flat, taste like they came straight from an orchard stand, and leave me with exactly one air fryer basket to wipe down. Total weeknight breakfast sanity saver.
ingredients: 1 can refrigerated buttermilk biscuits (Pillsbury Grands work best)
1 cup apple cider (reduced down to 3 tablespoons on the stove)
Cooking spray or avocado oil for the air fryer basket
instructions: Step 1: Pour your apple cider into a small saucepan and simmer over medium heat until it reduces down to about 3 tablespoons. It should look thick and syrupy—don't rush this or your dough gets soggy.

Step 2: Pop open your can of biscuits and separate them. Use a small bottle cap or a piping tip to cut a hole right out of the center of each round. Save those dough holes because they fry up into the best little donut bites!
Step 3: Preheat your air fryer to 350 degrees F. Lightly mist the basket with avocado oil. Place the donuts in a single layer without crowding—work in batches if your basket is small like mine.

Step 4: Air fry for 5 to 6 minutes until they puff up and turn golden brown. While they're still hot, brush them with the melted butter, dip them straight into your cinnamon-sugar mixture, and eat immediately.
proHack: Don't skip the cider reduction step! If you use straight liquid apple cider, the biscuit dough gets way too wet and won't puff up right in the air fryer. Boiling it down concentrates that tart apple flavor so it actually tastes like a real orchard donut.
storage: Honestly, these are best eaten the exact minute you make them while they're warm and crispy. If you somehow have extras, store them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one day. Reheat in the air fryer at 300 degrees F for 2 minutes to bring back that fresh-baked crunch.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the canned biscuits if I don't have them?
faqs.answer: You can totally use homemade quick-bread dough or even puff pastry squares, though the texture will be flakier and less like a traditional cake donut.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the donuts from sticking to the air fryer basket?
faqs.answer: Make sure to give your basket a quick spray with avocado oil or standard cooking spray before adding the dough. Avoid aerosol sprays with propellants like Pam if your basket has a delicate non-stick coating.
